one_liner: Cloud collaboration suite with a broad public HTTP OpenAPI using app id/secret and OAuth user tokens; whether a non-paying developer can create those credentials is not evidenced.

auth.notes: A custom app mints a tenant access token by POSTing its app id and app secret, and a separate OAuth flow exchanges a login authorization code for a user_access_token used to call APIs as the user. The user-token path is the one prescribed for acting on behalf of a user.

access.notes: Developer docs say to create an app and take the App ID and App Secret, and a free Starter plan is mentioned, but no readable sentence ties that plan or any other plan to OpenAPI calls or credential creation. Publishing a new app version is described as reviewed, but that claim could not be re-verified from a readable page.

api.notes: The official Node SDK documents server APIs as HTTP calls (domain plus /open-apis/..., method GET or POST, JSON body) covering messaging, calendars, documents, Base, contacts, approvals and application management. Linked reference pages are public and the SDK bundle is readable without logging in.

mcp.notes: Published by larksuite as @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp and documented on the Lark developer site. The GitHub README labels it Beta. A remote hosted MCP mode exists but the docs mark it Deprecated; the usable path is the local npm server.

verdict.rationale: The HTTP API is public, broad, and callable with app id/secret plus an OAuth user token, so the product is technically buildable. Access to credentials is unknown because the only pages that describe the free plan and the OpenAPI call limit are JavaScript-rendered and could not be re-read, so neither buildable_now nor a paid or partner gate can be proven.

problems: open.larksuite.com, open.feishu.cn and larksuite.com all render with JavaScript, so fetch_page failed on every official docs and pricing URL, and the paid Tavily budget was already zero, so none of those pages could be re-extracted.

The previous quotes about the free trial, the free Starter plan, the app-version review, and the user_access_token OAuth sentence therefore could not be re-verified and were dropped rather than repeated.
The pricing page's OpenAPI call-limit row still cannot be tied to a plan column.
GitHub code search requires a login, so I could not search the SDK repository; the evidence instead comes from the raw README and the published npm bundle.
